clue.text: Drawback in recession, maître d' is pilfering sandwiches

indicators.note: something in recession goes backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
to sandwich is to hold between two outer layers, so the wanted letters sit inside the surrounding words

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these words, ending inside the last one

explanation.surface: In hard times, a head waiter has been stealing sandwiches from the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the stolen food, but it is the verb that hides the letters; read backwards across 'maîtrE D' IS PILFering' they spell FLIPSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The flipside of something is its downside or less attractive aspect, a near synonym for a drawback.

clue.text: Scottish river houses really old — old-fashioned indeed

indicators.note: a building houses its occupants by holding them inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Forth flows into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh
really is SO, as in 'so good', and O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A Scottish river runs past something truly ancient, an archaic-sounding observation.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash separates wordplay from definition; 'old' appears twice, once as a letter and once inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic interjection meaning truly or in truth, now used only jokingly or in period writing.

clue.text: Enter hot place

parts.note: hot in the sense of fashionable or popular
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: An instruction to go into somewhere sweltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' reads as temperature but here means trendy, and 'place' is a verb, not a location.
explanation.definitionFit: To input data is to type or feed it into a computer, the same act as entering it.

clue.text: Band I'm in snubbed Japanese food

indicators.note: snubbed can mean cut short, like a snub nose, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
the word with its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A musician complains of being ignored while eating at a Japanese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' suggests being ignored socially; here it trims the tail of the little word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is a Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish, served without rice.

clue.text: Expected to join with student for fight

indicators.note: joining two things puts them side by side, so the pieces are simply placed one after another

parts.note: a baby or train that is due is expected
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Someone is anticipated to team up with a pupil for a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Student is L because a learner driver in Britain displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people, so it is a kind of fight.

clue.text: Changes plugs in apartment? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it
this flips the stated relation, so the holder and the thing held swap roles

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement
common abbreviation for apartment

explanation.surface: Someone rewires the electrical sockets in a flat, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugs in apartment' tells you to put the adverts inside the flat; 'Quite the opposite' reverses that, so the apartment goes inside the adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to alter or modify it to suit new conditions, so adapts means changes.

clue.text: Criminal has to enter party, and two females run away

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a do is an informal British word for a party

indicators.note: a criminal act is a crooked one, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled

explanation.surface: A crook gatecrashes a party and two women flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the person in the story; it is the signal to rearrange the next word. A do is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash off is to leave in a hurry, a phrasal verb equivalent to making a quick exit.

clue.text: Eschewing topping, wrap a pizza badly for flash-mob

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid, and in a down clue the topping is the first letter, so that letter is dropped
something done badly is messed up, so the letters end up jumbled

parts.note: the word without its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skips the toppings and wraps a pizza clumsily, maybe for a group stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' sounds like pizza cheese but means the top letter of the next word in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paparazzi are photographers who swarm celebrities, their camera flashes going off, so a mob with flashes is a witty description.

clue.text: Ringo's making one right international flight?

indicators.note: making one thing into another means changing it, so one letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer; add the possessive S
R is the abbreviation for right; this is the letter that goes
I is the abbreviation for international; this is the letter that comes in

explanation.surface: Ringo Starr seems to be catching a flight abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Rs in the drummer's surname is turned into an I. 'International flight' reads as air travel, but the question mark flags a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, so a staircase, rather than a journey by plane.

clue.text: Take back incorrectly ordered espressos

indicators.note: things placed in the wrong order have been mixed up, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A café customer returns coffees that came wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' in a café means requested, but here it is about arrangement of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to reclaim goods, typically when payments have lapsed, which is taking them back.

clue.text: Supports or tolerates Times

parts.note: as in 'I can't stand it'
multiplication: three times four is three by four

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a newspaper backs or merely puts up with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Times' look like the newspaper; it is the multiplication word, as in measurements of 'six by four'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand by someone is to remain loyal and give them backing in difficulty.

clue.text: Colour copies on the counter around one

indicators.note: counter suggests running against the usual direction, so the word is read backwards
to go around something is to enclose it

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Coloured photocopies are left lying on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' paints a shop scene but means counter-wise, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tone familiar from old photographs, originally an ink made from cuttlefish.

clue.text: Get combat rations regularly

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the alternation carries on: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An order to collect army field food on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting from the second letter of 'combat' and skipping one each time runs straight across into 'rations'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or come into possession of it, a formal equivalent of getting.

clue.text: Party conference — leader ultimately gets hand

parts.note: the Labour Party, one of Britain's two main parties

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: At the annual party conference, the leader finally receives a round of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party conference' looks like a single event, and 'hand' like applause; 'ultimately' acts on both 'conference' and 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand or factory hand, which is what a labourer is.

clue.text: Fight with current head leads to caution

parts.note: a war is a large-scale fight
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Fighting against the prevailing leader makes people careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current head' reads as the present leader; split them: current is I and head is NESS, a headland or promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness is the state of being on guard against danger, which is what caution means.

clue.text: Picture of what I froze — roughly about 500 ounces

indicators.note: roughly means carelessly and about means around, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500
oz is the standard abbreviation for ounces

explanation.surface: A photo of the food I put in the freezer, weighing around 500 ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a film, as in motion picture; the Roman numeral joins the anagram fodder before the abbreviation is tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1939 musical film starring Judy Garland is a classic Hollywood motion picture.

clue.text: Former spouse ringing, celebrating

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
a bell tolls when it rings slowly

explanation.surface: An ex-partner phones to share some happy news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' suggests a phone call; here it is the slow ringing of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Extolling means praising enthusiastically, and to celebrate someone's achievements is to praise them publicly.

clue.text: Transfer goods from the south, beginning with electronic kitchen gadget

indicators.note: beginning with something means having it placed at the front

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom upward runs the letters backwards

parts.note: to remit money is to transfer it
G is the abbreviation for good, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Shipping merchandise up from the south, starting with an electronic kitchen appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goods' looks like merchandise, but it is two abbreviations for good; the reversed block then gets the electronic letter in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer is a small kitchen device, often a sandglass, for timing boiled eggs.

clue.text: Sport with lanes in PE with Bolt winning stupidly …

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school PE lesson in which the sprinter Usain Bolt keeps winning, absurdly, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport with lanes' sounds like athletics, which fits Bolt, but the lanes are bowling alleys. PE is physical education, the school sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenpin bowling is played by rolling balls down long wooden lanes at ten pins.

clue.text: Pasta in new bags

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
bags of something means lots of it, as does oodles

explanation.surface: Pasta packed into fresh bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link here, not an instruction to put one thing inside another; 'bags' is British informal for lots.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long strips of dough, the Asian cousin of Italian pasta and often counted as a type of it.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well? Used to be — but over the hill finally

parts.note: the past tense of 'is'

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A former good-for-nothing who is now simply past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like the conjunction tying the halves together, yet it is the first of four words whose final letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle, wasteful person who never makes good, the same as a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Women's group, having rushed around, made a decision on Tinder

indicators.note: to have something around you is to hold it inside

parts.note: to speed is to rush
the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: A women's club hurriedly picks a date on a dating app.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British organisation famous for jam and charity work.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dating app Tinder, users swipe right or left to accept or reject a profile.

clue.text: .. easy victory, with a fan keeping close to track

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold onto it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
a fan of jazz is a jazz lover

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Continuing the bowling scene: a win made easy, with a supporter staying near the track.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots pick up from 18 across, where Bolt was winning stupidly.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is a contest won with no effort, originally a race where the only runner could simply walk the course.

clue.text: Take out key men before time

parts.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard
other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An order to eliminate the important people ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key men' reads as vital personnel; split it into a keyboard key and the military abbreviation for men.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany them, as when taking a partner out on a date.

clue.text: Bulb working — one that's electrically charged

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A light bulb is functioning, which is to say it carries a current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' and 'electrically' point to a lamp; the definition is the vegetable sort of bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion grows as an underground bulb of layered leaves, so it is a bulb in the botanical sense.

clue.text: Reportedly bet against

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: an ante is a stake put into the pot in poker

explanation.walkthrough: The poker stake and the prefix are pronounced the same in many accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is anti a proposal opposes it, a colloquial preposition meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Greek character with a large bottle

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A Greek man carrying a big bottle, perhaps of ouzo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass vial for medicine or perfume, a kind of little bottle.

clue.text: Giro money's so wasted — loves going out — it's better with others

indicators.note: wasted can mean drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order
things going out leave the room, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O, so several loves are several Os

explanation.surface: Benefit money gets squandered and romance fades, though life is better shared.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro was a British state benefit cheque. Remove the three Os from the fodder before rearranging what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergism is the effect where combined parts achieve more together than separately, so a thing works better in company.

clue.text: Understand mine is in Paris

parts.note: to mine is to dig, and a dig is also an excavation
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A puzzled grasp of whether something belonging to me is in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive; it is the verb meaning to excavate.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to absorb and comprehend it fully, a figurative sense of digesting food.

clue.text: Plastic bag from container ship

parts.note: a bin is a container for rubbish
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A plastic bag has come off a container vessel, suggesting ocean pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container ship' reads as one cargo vessel; split it into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: A bin-liner is a plastic sack used to line a rubbish bin, the British term for a garbage bag.
